main_text.l: Coronam à capite, Sceptrum e manu
stomus, licèt in sua causa certè reclamasset,
ex Homilia de Dauid & Saul innotefcit:
in quo [?] eloquentiæ quasi torrente audi-
ctatus est Dauid, pugilem egit, iracundia
Deus: quin potiùs non ipsi modò
aduersus seipsum erat prælium, sed aduer-

page.notes: Left page: the margin notes are "f Lib.6. cap.10.", "t Lib.8. c.27.& 28." and "u Jn c.13." ("Jn" is doubtful, possibly "In"). The text has no further notes. Marks f, t and u correspond to "Socrate", "Sozomeno" and "Romanos" in the text. The word after "in quo" is partly covered by a dark smudge and is doubtful. "Eudoxiä" is uncertain for the final mark. The first paragraph starts at the top of the column without an indent, so it continues from the previous page. The last text line "sus" completes the hyphenated word "aduer-" and is part of the text. Right page: only the line-beginnings at the scan edge are visible; the list above gives those fragments as they appear, and the rest of that page is not legible.
